mainTopic: The כיפה for repeat sinners and unconvictable killers, and the משנה of sinners whom קנאין may strike
overview: The amud opens with the last line of the previous discussion: רבא tells רב אדא that a person cannot be killed with two death penalties. A new משנה then teaches that someone who was given מלקות and sinned again is locked in the כיפה and fed barley until he dies. ריש לקיש explains that this applies only to כרת sins, where the sinner already deserves death and has given up on his life. רבי יעקב narrows it further to repeating the same כרת sin. The גמרא then asks how many times are needed before the כיפה, using two ברייתות where the חכמים say three times and אבא שאול says four. It also describes the כיפה as a cell the person's exact height. A second משנה puts a killer who cannot be convicted for lack of valid witnesses into the כיפה, and the גמרא gives three ways the court could know he killed, then explains how the diets in the two משניות fit together. Finally, a third משנה lists sinners whom קנאין may strike, a כהן who served while טמא, and a זר who served. The גמרא explains קסוה and the curse 'with a קוסם', and begins a question from רב כהנא about the ארמית that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא: You Cannot Kill a Person Twice
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the idea that one person could get two death penalties, and so closes the previous discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: אדא, my son, will you kill him with two death penalties?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the earlier discussion. רבא pushes back on רב אדא by pointing out that you cannot execute a person twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if two prohibitions apply to the same act, a person can only die once. So when the sin was done on purpose, having a second death penalty adds nothing in practice. The question is rhetorical: it is a rejection, not a real request for information.

keyTerms.meaning: אדא, my son (a warm way of addressing a student)

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the discussion that came before. It is not part of the new משנה that follows.

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him: Adda, my son,
will you kill him with two death penalties?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַדָּא בְּרִי, בִּתְרֵי קְטָלֵי קָטְלַתְּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion, which began in the earlier part of the daf.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that a second death penalty has any practical effect when the sin was done on purpose.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A person can only be executed once, so two death penalties cannot both be carried out.

steps.title: משנה: One Who Was Flogged and Sinned Again Is Put in the כיפה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who was given מלקות and repeated the sin is placed in a closed cell and fed barley until he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who was flogged and then sinned again: בית דין puts him into the כיפה and feeds him barley until his belly bursts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It teaches a very harsh rule for someone who was given מלקות and then went back and did the sin again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a sin that is punished with מלקות does not lead to death by בית דין. Here the משנה says that repeating the sin can lead to the כיפה, a narrow cell where he is fed poor food until he dies. Right away this raises the question of why repeating a sin would be punished so severely.

keyTerms.meaning: was flogged and did it again

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the few cases where בית דין can bring about a death even though it is not one of the regular four death penalties.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who was flogged and repeated (the sin),
the court places him into the vaulted chamber,
and they feed him barley
until his belly bursts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the end of the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who was given מלקות and repeated the sin is put in the כיפה and fed barley until he dies.

steps.title: Why Such a Harsh Punishment for Repeating a Sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that simply sinning again after מלקות could lead to the כיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Just because he was flogged and did it again, בית דין puts him into the כיפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. It asks how repeating a sin that is only worth מלקות could lead to such a deadly punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin itself only carries מלקות, not death. So it seems out of proportion for בית דין to bring about his death just because he did it a second time. The גמרא needs to explain what makes this person deserve death.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: Because he was flogged and repeated (the sin),
the court places him into the vaulted chamber?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָקָה וְשָׁנָה, בֵּית דִּין כּוֹנְסִין אוֹתוֹ לַכִּיפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the harshness of the rule in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a repeat offender is put in the כיפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sin that only carries מלקות should not lead to death, even if it is repeated.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: The Case Is Lashes for כרת Sins
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the משנה is talking about sins that carry כרת, so the person is already liable to death and has shown he does not care about his life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: Here we are dealing with lashes for sins that carry כרת. This man already deserves death; it is just that his death is not being brought closer. Since he is giving up on his own life, we bring his death closer upon him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה, quoting ריש לקיש, answers the challenge. The משנה is only talking about sins that carry כרת, which already make the person liable to death from Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who did a כרת sin already 'deserves death'. The only thing missing is that nobody is speeding up that death. By sinning again after מלקות, he shows he has given up on his own life, so בית דין speeds up a death he already deserves. The כיפה is not a brand-new death sentence.

keyTerms.meaning: lashes given for sins that carry כרת
he gives up on his own life

steps.whatToRemember: The כיפה only applies to sins that carry כרת. Because the sinner already deserves death from Heaven, בית דין is only speeding up that death after he shows he has given up on his life.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the כיפה is not out of proportion: the death was already deserved, and בית דין only brings it sooner.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Here we are dealing with lashes for (sins of) karet,
since the man is (already) liable to death,
phrases.notes: He means death from Heaven, which is what כרת is.

phrases.english: it is just that his death has not been brought closer.
And since he gives up on his own life,
we bring his death closer upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by limiting the משנה to כרת sins.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case in the משנה (אוקימתא) to sins that carry כרת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to apply to any sin punished with מלקות, which would make the כיפה far too harsh.
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies only to כרת sins, where the person already deserves death, and בית דין only speeds it up.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: Only When It Is the Same כרת Sin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב narrows the rule: the כיפה applies only when he repeats one כרת sin, not when he does two or three different ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said to רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא: Come, I will explain it to you. This is about lashes for one כרת sin. But if it was two or three different כרת sins, he is just tasting different prohibitions, and he is not giving up on his life that much.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב adds a limit to ריש לקיש's explanation. The כיפה is only for someone who keeps repeating the same כרת sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating the very same sin shows he truly does not care about his life. Doing different כרת sins could just be wanting to try the 'taste' of different forbidden things. That is not the same level of giving up on his life, so he is not put in the כיפה.

keyTerms.meaning: come, I will explain it to you
that much, to such a degree

steps.whatToRemember: The כיפה applies only to someone who repeats the same כרת sin. Doing different כרת sins does not count, because that is seen as 'tasting' different sins rather than giving up on his life.
steps.confusionAlert: It may seem that doing more kinds of כרת sins is worse. But here the deciding factor is whether he has given up on his life, and that shows most clearly when he repeats the very same sin.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said
to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Tachlifa:
Come, I will explain it to you,
(it is) with lashes for one (sin of) karet,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שֶׁל שְׁתַּיִם וְשֶׁל שָׁלֹשׁ כָּרֵיתוֹת –
phrases.english: but (lashes) for two or three (different) karet sins –
it is prohibitions that he is tasting,
and he is not giving up (on his life) that much.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא אַסְבְּרָא לָךְ, בְּמַלְקִיּוֹת שֶׁל כָּרֵת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows ריש לקיש's answer to the case of one כרת sin repeated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כיפה applies only to repeating one כרת sin. Different כרת sins are 'tasting' prohibitions and do not show the same giving up on life.

steps.title: Does our משנה go against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה again and points out that the כיפה comes after only a second time. That seems to go against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who holds that a חזקה is only made after three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'one who was given lashes and repeated.' This means once he repeats, even without a third time. So shall we say our משנה does not follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל? He says there is no חזקה until something happens three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the words of the משנה and asks whether the משנה disagrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's words 'לקה ושנה' make it sound like a second sin is enough for the כיפה. But the כיפה is for someone who has become an established sinner, a חזקה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a חזקה needs three times, so the משנה seems not to fit his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say: a suggestion the גמרא puts forward, often to be rejected
An established pattern or status, here being a confirmed repeat sinner

phrases.english: One who was given lashes and repeated.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁנָה אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא שִׁילֵּשׁ.
phrases.english: Once he repeated, even though he did not do it a third time.

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל?
phrases.english: Shall we say our משנה is not like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?
For if it were Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
doesn't he say:

phrases.aramaic: עַד תְּלָת זִימְנֵי לָא הָוְיָא חֲזָקָה.
phrases.english: Until three times, there is no established status.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה from step 2 and checks how its wording fits a known תנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the כיפה comes after 'לקה ושנה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה seems to make the sinner an established sinner after two times, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires three times for any חזקה.

steps.title: רבינא: count the sins, not the lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the משנה can follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, because what builds the חזקה is the sins themselves, not the lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: You can even say it follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He holds that sins are what create the חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends the משנה. He shows that it can still match רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed we count the lashes: lashed once, then repeating would be only time two. רבינא says we count the sins. He sinned, sinned again, and with the next sin he has three sins, which is a full חזקה even by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say: the case can fit even this opinion
Sins establish the חזקה: we count the number of sins

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying two times is enough. He agrees three times are needed. He only changes what we count: sins instead of lashes.

phrases.english: Ravina said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: You can even say it is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
for he holds that sins establish the status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what is being counted toward the חזקה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lashes are what count, so the משנה gives a חזקה after only two and must disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sins are what count, so three sins give a חזקה, which fits רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to show everyone counts the lashes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. The חכמים say the כיפה comes the third time, and אבא שאול says the fourth time. The גמרא suggests both sides count lashes and are simply repeating the argument between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: If someone did a sin that carries lashes, the first and second time they lash him, and the third time they put him into the כיפה. אבא שאול says: even the third time they lash him, and the fourth time they put him into the כיפה. Isn't it that everyone holds the lashes create the חזקה, and they are arguing the same point that רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבינא's idea that we count sins and not lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both sides count lashes, then the חכמים (two lashes, then the כיפה) hold like רבי, who says two times make a חזקה. אבא שאול (three lashes) holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. That would mean nobody who follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל counts sins, and the opinion that matches our משנה belongs to רבי, not to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא
Lashes establish the חזקה: we count the number of times he was lashed
Isn't it that...? A suggested reading the גמרא proposes

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If one did a sin that carries lashes,
the first time and the second time they lash him,
and the third time they put him into the closed cell.
Abba Shaul says:
Even the third time they lash him,
and the fourth time they put him into the closed cell.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מַלְקִיּוֹת מַחְזִיקוֹת,
phrases.english: Isn't it that everyone holds the lashes establish the status,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל קָמִיפַּלְגִי?
phrases.english: and they argue the same dispute as Rebbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?
phrases.notes: רבי holds two times are enough for a חזקה, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds three.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: עָבַר עֲבֵירָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ מַלְקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's answer from step 7 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל could count sins rather than lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The easiest reading of the ברייתא is that both sides count lashes and only argue over two or three times. That would make the view matching our משנה follow רבי, not רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Both sides follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל but count differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that everyone in the ברייתא agrees to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's three times. The חכמים count sins, and אבא שאול counts lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Here they argue about this: one Sage holds that sins create the חזקה, and the other Sage holds that lashes create the חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the challenge and rereads the ברייתא so that it supports רבינא's idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים count sins: by the third sin he has three, so he goes to the כיפה. אבא שאול counts lashes: he needs three lashings first, so only the fourth sin brings the כיפה. So the 'count the sins' view that רבינא needed really does exist alongside רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: One Sage... and the other Sage

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone can agree that a חזקה needs three times. The question is what we count. If we count sins (the חכמים, and our משנה according to רבינא), the כיפה comes at the third sin. If we count lashes (אבא שאול), it comes at the fourth sin.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: No, everyone holds like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and here this is what they argue about:
one Sage holds that sins establish the status,
phrases.notes: This is the first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא: the כיפה at the third time.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds that lashes establish the status.
phrases.notes: This is אבא שאול: the כיפה at the fourth time.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns away the challenge of step 8 and upholds רבינא from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the dispute in the ברייתא as a different argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's dispute is רבי against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, with both sides counting lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sides follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. They argue whether sins or lashes are counted, which confirms that the 'count the sins' view exists.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה can follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל if we count sins, as the חכמים in the ברייתא do.

steps.title: A case with no lashes still has the same third-or-fourth dispute
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the same dispute between the חכמים (third time) and אבא שאול (fourth time) in a case where the sinner never accepted the warning, so no lashes were given. If no lashes were given, אבא שאול cannot be counting lashes. So what is the argument about?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a ברייתא: if they warned him and he stayed silent, or they warned him and he only nodded his head, then the first and second time they warn him, and the third time they put him into the כיפה. אבא שאול says: even the third time they warn him, and the fourth time they put him into the כיפה. In that case there are no lashes at all. So what are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to break the answer from Step 9, because in this case nobody gets lashes. It then asks what the two sides are really arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said אבא שאול reaches 'fourth time' by counting lashes. Here the sinner never clearly accepted the warning, so lashes are never given, yet אבא שאול still says 'fourth time.' His view must rest on something other than counting lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: They warned him (the witnesses told him the sin and its punishment beforehand)
And he bowed or nodded his head (he did not clearly say he accepted the warning)
They bring him in, they put him into

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the earlier ברייתא in Step 8. The two sides and the numbers are the same, but the case is different. Here the sinner never clearly accepted the warning, so there are no lashes to count.

phrases.english: But what about that which is taught: they warned him and he was silent,
or they warned him and he nodded his head –
the first and second time, they warn him,
the third time, they put him into the כיפה.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: אַף בַּשְּׁלִישִׁית מַתְרִין בּוֹ,
phrases.english: אבא שאול says: even the third time they warn him,
and the fourth time, they put him into the כיפה.
And there, there are no lashes.
So about what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 9's answer that אבא שאול counts lashes.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 9's claim that אבא שאול reaches 'fourth time' by counting lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same dispute appears in a case with no lashes at all, so counting lashes cannot explain אבא שאול's 'fourth time.'

steps.title: רבינא: they argue whether the כיפה needs its own warning
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the dispute is about whether the person must be warned specifically about the כיפה before he can be put there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: they disagree about whether the כיפה requires a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question by naming the real point of the argument: does the כיפה need its own separate warning?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים hold that no special warning is needed, so after three times he goes straight into the כיפה. אבא שאול holds that he must first be warned about the כיפה itself, which pushes it to the fourth time. This works whether or not lashes were ever given.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question
A warning given before the sin

steps.whatToRemember: In the ברייתא where no lashes are given, the third-or-fourth dispute is about whether the כיפה needs its own warning. The חכמים say no, so he goes in the third time. אבא שאול says yes, so he goes in the fourth time.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the dispute in the second ברייתא, where there are no lashes at all. There, אבא שאול's 'fourth time' comes from the extra warning about the כיפה. The גמרא does not take back its reading of the first ברייתא from Step 9.

phrases.english: רבינא said:
They disagree about whether the כיפה requires a warning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: בְּכִיפָּה צְרִיכָה הַתְרָאָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the dispute is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following step 9, אבא שאול's fourth time seemed to come from counting lashes, which cannot work in a case with no lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the second ברייתא, the dispute is whether the כיפה needs its own warning. אבא שאול requires one, which adds a time.

steps.title: What exactly is the כיפה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the כיפה actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the כיפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question and asks for a description of the כיפה. It is setting up רב יהודה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא has spoken about when a person is put into the כיפה. Now it wants to know what the כיפה itself is.

keyTerms.meaning: A vaulted cell where a repeat sinner is locked up

phrases.english: And what is the כיפה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from when the כיפה is used to what it is.

steps.title: רב יהודה: a cell exactly his full height
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the כיפה is a space exactly the person's full height.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: it is the full size of his height.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question: the כיפה is a tiny cell built exactly to the person's height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because it fits him exactly, he cannot move around inside it. This makes it a very harsh punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: The full size of his height

phrases.english: רב יהודה said: the full size of his height.
phrases.notes: A tiny cell exactly his size, so he can't move around in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כיפה is a space exactly the person's height.

steps.title: Where is the כיפה hinted at in the פסוקים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the punishment of the כיפה is hinted at in the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is it hinted at?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source in the פסוקים for the כיפה. It is setting up ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not ask for a full proof, only for a hint (רמז). It wants to show that this punishment has a root in the פסוקים.

phrases.english: And where is it hinted at?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the כיפה, asks for its hint in the פסוקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that hints at the כיפה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: 'Evil shall kill the wicked'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש brings the פסוק 'Evil shall kill the wicked' as the hint for the כיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: 'Evil shall kill the wicked.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers with a פסוק from תהלים as the hint for the כיפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that the wicked person's own evil brings about his death. The כיפה is a death brought on by his repeated sins, so the פסוק hints at it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, רבי שמעון בן לקיש

steps.whatToRemember: The כיפה is a cell exactly the sinner's height (רב יהודה), and it is hinted at in 'Evil shall kill the wicked' (ריש לקיש).

phrases.english: ריש לקיש said:
'Evil shall kill the wicked.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: תְּמוֹתֵת רָשָׁע רָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hint is the פסוק 'Evil shall kill the wicked.'

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks what the 'evil net' in a פסוק is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another teaching of ריש לקיש. He quotes a פסוק comparing people to fish caught in an 'evil net' and asks what that net is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: What is the meaning of what is written, 'For man also does not know his time, like fish that are caught in an evil net'? What is the 'evil net'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching of ריש לקיש, who quotes a פסוק and asks what its 'evil net' means. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching sits next to the previous one because it also comes from ריש לקיש and also uses the word 'evil' (רעה). The question is narrow: what kind of net is called 'evil'?

phrases.english: And ריש לקיש said: What is the meaning of what is written,
'For man also does not know his time,
phrases.notes: קהלת 9:12. The word in square brackets, גם, is part of the corrected wording, so the line matches the פסוק.

phrases.english: like fish that are caught in an evil net'?
What is the 'evil net'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching of ריש לקיש, linked by the word 'evil.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the 'evil net' in the פסוק is.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the 'evil net' is a hook
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the 'evil net' is a fishhook.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: a hook.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers his own question: the 'evil net' in the פסוק is a fishhook.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'evil net' as a hook rather than a normal net. That is the whole answer the גמרא gives here.

phrases.english: ריש לקיש said: a hook.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16.

steps.title: New משנה: a killer without witnesses is placed in the כיפה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who killed without witnesses is put in the כיפה and given sparse bread and scant water.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone kills a person and there are no proper witnesses, the court puts him into the כיפה and feeds him a tiny amount of bread and water.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It says that a killer who cannot be convicted through normal witnesses is locked in the כיפה and fed very little.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a murderer is executed only through valid witnesses and a full trial. This משנה deals with a killer who escapes that process, and it gives the court a way to deal with him anyway. It uses the same כיפה that the previous steps described.

keyTerms.meaning: A small chamber exactly the person's height

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who kills a person not in front of witnesses,
they put him into the vaulted chamber

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ לֶחֶם צָר וּמַיִם לָחַץ.
phrases.english: and feed him sparse bread and scant water.
phrases.notes: This wording comes from a פסוק: ישעיהו 30:20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה that uses the כיפה defined in earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A killer who cannot be convicted for lack of proper witnesses is put in the כיפה and given sparse bread and scant water.

steps.title: How do we know he killed at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if there were no witnesses, how does the court know he is a killer?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a basic question about the משנה. If nobody witnessed the killing, how can the court be sure enough to punish him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's words 'not in front of witnesses' seem to leave no evidence at all. The גמרא is setting up the next steps, which explain that there was evidence that was simply not legally valid.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
How do we know?
phrases.notes: He means: if there were no witnesses, how do we even know he killed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case described in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of case is meant, where the court knows he killed but there were 'no witnesses'?

steps.title: רב: the witnesses saw it separately
steps.stepSummary: רב says the case involves עדות מיוחדת, where each witness saw the killing on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It is a case of separated testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that there were witnesses, but they did not see the killing together. So their testimony cannot be combined to convict him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court can tell the witnesses are telling the truth, but halacha needs the witnesses to see together for a death penalty. So 'without witnesses' really means 'without legally valid witnesses.'

keyTerms.meaning: Separated testimony: each witness saw the event alone

steps.confusionAlert: 'Without witnesses' does not mean nobody saw anything. It means there was no testimony good enough for a death sentence.

phrases.english: Rav said: with separated testimony.
phrases.notes: Each witness saw the killing alone, not together with the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The witnesses saw the killing separately, so their testimony cannot convict him.

steps.title: שמואל: he was never warned
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the case is one where valid witnesses saw it, but there was no התראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: It is a case where he was not warned.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different answer. The witnesses did see the killing, but nobody warned the killer beforehand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A court cannot execute someone unless he was warned before the act. Here the facts are clear, but this missing step blocks the death penalty, so the court uses the כיפה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning given before the crime, needed for court punishment

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: without a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question of step 19, different from רב's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The witnesses saw the killing, but he was not warned, so he cannot be executed.

steps.title: אבימי: witnesses contradicted only on side details
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes אבימי: the witnesses contradicted each other in the בדיקות but agreed in the חקירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי: For example, where the witnesses contradicted each other in the side-detail questions, but not in the main questions.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer. The witnesses agreed on the key facts but contradicted each other on small side details, which disqualifies their testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חקירות are the core questions, like the time and place, and the בדיקות are side details. A contradiction in the side details voids the testimony legally. But since they agreed on the core facts, the court knows he is guilty.

keyTerms.meaning: Interrogations about core facts like time and place

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said in the name of Avimi:
for example, where they were contradicted in the side-detail examinations
but were not contradicted in the core interrogations,
phrases.notes: The core questions are about when and where it happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third answer to step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The witnesses agreed on the core facts but contradicted each other on side details, so their testimony is void while the guilt is clear.

steps.title: Example of side-detail questions: בן זכאי and the fig stems
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to an earlier משנה where בן זכאי questioned witnesses about the stems of figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: There was an incident, and בן זכאי examined the witnesses about the stems of the figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up אבימי's idea of 'side details' with an earlier משנה. בן זכאי asked the witnesses about the fig stems, a side detail of the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that בדיקות really exist as a type of questioning, and that witnesses can be tested on small details. It gives a clear picture of what a 'side-detail' contradiction looks like.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Three ways to know he killed without valid testimony: witnesses saw separately (רב), no warning (שמואל), or contradictions only in side details (אבימי).

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
There was an incident, and Ben Zakkai examined the witnesses
about the stems of the figs.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on daf 40a; he asked about the fig tree where the killing happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and illustrates אבימי's case of בדיקות.
steps.raayaObject: That witnesses are questioned on side details (בדיקות), as אבימי described.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (40a) where בן זכאי examined witnesses about the fig stems.

steps.title: Two משניות describe different food in the כיפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this משנה says sparse bread and water, while the previous משנה says barley until his belly bursts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And they feed him sparse bread and scant water.' Why does it teach here that they give him sparse bread and scant water, while there it teaches that they feed him barley until his belly bursts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of our משנה. It notices that the previous משנה describes a different diet in the כיפה, and asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both משניות deal with the כיפה, but one mentions a starvation diet and the other mentions barley that bursts the belly. This looks like two different punishments, and the גמרא wants to know how they fit together.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ לֶחֶם צָר וּמַיִם לָחַץ.
phrases.english: And they feed him sparse bread and scant water.
What is different here, that it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתְנִין לוֹ לֶחֶם צָר וּמַיִם לָחַץ,
phrases.english: they give him sparse bread and scant water,
and what is different there, that it teaches:
phrases.notes: 'There' is the previous משנה, about the repeat sinner put in the כיפה.

phrases.english: they feed him barley
until his belly bursts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second half of the משנה and compares it to the previous משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two משניות describing the diet in the כיפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both deal with the same כיפה, yet one says sparse bread and water and the other says barley until the belly bursts, which seems like a contradiction.

steps.title: רב ששת: one process in two stages
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says both happen: first the starvation diet shrinks his intestines, and then barley bursts his belly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: In both cases, they first give him sparse bread and scant water until his intestines shrink, and then they feed him barley until his belly bursts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers that there is no contradiction. The two משניות describe two stages of the same punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The starvation diet comes first and shrinks his insides. Then the barley expands inside him and bursts his belly. Each משנה mentions only one stage, but both stages apply in both cases.
steps.whatToRemember: The two משניות do not argue: the כיפה punishment is sparse bread and water first, then barley.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
In both this case and that case,

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתְנִין לוֹ לֶחֶם צָר וּמַיִם לָחַץ
phrases.english: they give him sparse bread and scant water
until his intestines shrink,
and then they feed him barley
until his belly bursts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: both sources describe stages of one process.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות describe two different punishments in the כיפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is one punishment: first sparse bread and water, then barley until the belly bursts.

steps.title: Three sinners whom zealots may strike
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three people whom קנאין may strike: one who steals a קסוה, one who curses with a קוסם, and one who has relations with an ארמית.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who steals the קסוה, one who curses with a sorcerer, and one who has relations with an Aramean woman: zealots strike him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It names three sins where a zealous person may strike the sinner even without a בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are not ordinary court death penalties. The law here allows a קנאי, someone acting out of zeal for ה׳, to act on his own. The גמרא will explain each of the three cases one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel; the גמרא will define it
Zealots: people acting out of zeal for ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a punishment that בית דין carries out. It is permission for a קנאי to act on his own.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who steals the kasva
and one who curses with a sorcerer
and one who has relations with an Aramean woman
zealots strike him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of כיפה ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In three specific sins, קנאין may strike the sinner.

steps.title: A priest who served while impure
steps.stepSummary: A כהן who served while טמא is not brought to בית דין. Instead, the young כהנים take him out of the עזרה and split his skull with pieces of wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן who served while impure: his fellow כהנים do not bring him to court. Rather, the young כהנים take him outside the courtyard and split his skull with pieces of wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case. A כהן did the עבודה while he was טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As with the קנאין, this is handled outside the normal court process. The young כהנים deal with him directly, outside the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Did the Temple service while ritually impure
Young כהנים, literally 'blossoms of the priesthood'

phrases.english: A kohen who served while impure

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים מְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ לְבֵית דִּין
phrases.english: his brother kohanim do not bring him to court

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא פִּרְחֵי כְהוּנָּה מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ חוּץ לָעֲזָרָה
phrases.english: rather, the young kohanim take him out of the courtyard
and split his skull with pieces of wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the משנה that is also handled without a בית דין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who served while טמא is struck by the young כהנים outside the עזרה, not judged in court.

steps.title: A non-priest who served in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: For a זר who served in the מקדש, רבי עקיבא says the punishment is חנק, and חכמים say it is death בידי שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-כהן who served in the Temple: רבי עקיבא says he is killed by strangulation, and the Sages say he dies at the hands of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת about a זר who did the עבודה in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that בית דין executes him with חנק. חכמים hold that בית דין does not execute him at all, and his death comes from Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: At the hands of Heaven, not by בית דין

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three parts: קנאין for three sins, the young כהנים for a טמא כהן, and a מחלוקת about a זר.

phrases.english: A non-kohen who served in the Temple
Rabbi Akiva says: by strangulation
and the Sages say: at the hands of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case of the משנה, presented as a מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: חנק. חכמים: בידי שמים.

steps.title: What is a קסוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the word קסוה in the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is a קסוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a simple question about a word in the משנה. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קסוה is an unusual word. Before discussing the law, the גמרא first needs to know what object the משנה is talking about.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is a kasva?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the first case of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word קסוה.

steps.title: רב יהודה: a service vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that קסוה means a כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is a service vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question: a קסוה is a vessel used in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the first case is clear. It is a person who steals a holy vessel from the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel used for the Temple service

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: a service vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.

steps.title: A verse uses the same word for Temple vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב יהודה with a פסוק that calls the libation vessels קשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it says: 'And the jars of libation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to show that this word is used for Temple vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קשות in the פסוק sounds like קסוה. Since the פסוק uses it for the vessels of the נסכים, it supports reading קסוה as a כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says: brings a supporting פסוק

phrases.english: And so it says:
"And the jars of libation"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's definition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'ואת קשות הנסך' in במדבר.

steps.title: Where is this punishment hinted at?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the תורה hints that one who steals a כלי שרת may be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is it hinted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source in the תורה for this punishment. This sets up the פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה never says outright that this thief may be killed. So the גמרא looks for at least a hint (רמז) in a פסוק.

phrases.english: And where is it hinted?
phrases.notes: He means: where does the תורה hint that someone who steals a כלי שרת may be killed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the object, asks for the source of the law.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק hinting at death for stealing a כלי שרת.

steps.title: The verse of 'swallowing' the holy things
steps.stepSummary: The hint is the פסוק saying they must not see the holy things כבלע, or they will die.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They shall not come to see the holy things as they are covered, lest they die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that links the holy vessels with death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads כבלע as 'swallowing,' meaning taking the holy vessels. The words 'and they will die' then hint at death for one who steals them.

phrases.english: "And they shall not come to see
as the holy things are covered, lest they die."
phrases.notes: במדבר 4:20. The גמרא reads כְּבַלַּע as 'swallowing' the holy vessels, meaning stealing them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יָבֹאוּ לִרְאוֹת כְּבַלַּע אֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ וָמֵתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'ולא יבאו לראות כבלע את הקדש ומתו'.

steps.title: רב יוסף: let the sorcerer strike his sorcerer
steps.stepSummary: On the case of 'one who curses with a קוסם,' רב יוסף teaches that it means saying 'let the קוסם strike his קוסם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one who curses with a sorcerer.' רב יוסף taught: one who says, 'Let the sorcerer strike his sorcerer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second case in the משנה and quotes רב יוסף's explanation of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curse avoids saying ה׳'s name and instead uses the word קוסם. 'His קוסם' refers to the One the קוסם thinks gives him his power, so this is really a curse against ה׳ in disguise.

phrases.english: "And one who curses with a sorcerer."
Rav Yosef taught:
"Let the sorcerer strike his sorcerer."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first case of the משנה to the second.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cursing with a קוסם means saying 'יכה קוסם את קוסמו.'

steps.title: The Rabbis: strike him, his Creator and his Provider
steps.stepSummary: רבנן, or some say רבה בר מרי, explain the curse as 'let the קוסם strike him, his Creator, and his Provider.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis, and some say רבה בר מרי, say: 'Let the sorcerer strike him, and his Creator, and his Provider.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second explanation of the same case is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the person curses someone he is fighting with, and he openly includes that person's Creator, meaning ה׳. In both explanations the curse is aimed at ה׳. They differ only in the exact wording.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the curse, and both target ה׳ without saying His name directly.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּנַן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי, אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: The Rabbis, and some say Rabba bar Mari, say:
"Let the sorcerer strike him"
him, and his Creator, and his Provider.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי, אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative explanation to רב יוסף's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The curse is 'יכהו קוסם לו ולקונו ולמקנו.'

steps.title: רב כהנא begins asking רב about the Aramean woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the third case, הבועל ארמית, and introduces a question that רב כהנא asked רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one who has relations with an Aramean woman': רב כהנא asked of רב:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא moves to the third case, and the question itself comes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening of רב כהנא's question appears here. The question itself continues on the next amud.

Rav Kahana asked of Rav:
